text:
Noah (sales): Helix asked for a concise capacity plan for their enterprise commit. They said: ~2k qps peak (chat + embeddings), highly bursty around marketing blasts. Need reserved GPU recommendation, autoscale policy, burst-credit estimate, and security answers.
Ivy (solutions): Do we have their burst profile? predictable windows or fully ad-hoc?
Helix PM: Mostly predictable (campaigns) but sometimes ad-hoc. Baseline ~90 rps, spikes to ~2000 qps for 8-25m, ~12 events/month. Embeddings-heavy during ingestion windows.
Marco (eng-infra): Quick mapping using redwood-llama-8b-q mixed profile -> effective mixed throughput ~260 qps/node. For 2k peak that's ~8 nodes. Recommend 9 reserved if they want 10% headroom and AZ spread. Otherwise 5 reserved + autoscale to 14 covers most cases.
Tessa (sre): Note: coldstart + model load + KV population can add 4-35s tail latency. For user-facing chat this is noticeable. Mitigations: scheduled warm-starts, fast warm containers, and tiny standby traces.
Noah (sales): Helix wants a trio of options to show finance: fully reserved, hybrid (partial reserve + burst credits), and committed-minimum with burst credits. Also they asked how to price burst credits.
Marco (eng-infra): Pricing example (back-of-envelope): assume extra replica cost ~= $0.13/min. If during a 20m blast they need +6 replicas -> 6 * 0.13 * 20 = $31.2 per blast. At 12 blasts/mo -> ~$374/mo extra. I'll run sim with their trace for precise numbers.
Ivy (solutions): Can we give a sample autoscale policy and a CLI warm command to include in the SOW?
Marco (eng-infra): Yes. Example autoscale snippet (abbrev):
```
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 5
  max_replicas: 14
  target_rps_per_replica: 130
  scale_cooldown_s: 45
  prewarm_hook: /ops/warm --model=redwood-llama-8b-q --prefixes=top500 --parallel=6 --tokens=800k
```
Warm CLI:
```
./warm --model redwood-llama-8b-q --prefix-file frequent_prompts.txt --parallel 6 --duration 300
```
Tessa (sre): Add fallback policy: on >3 startup failures within 10m, divert traffic to quantized-compatible fallback model in-region and trigger on-call. Include acceptance of potential minor output drift in contract.
Lena (security): Dedicated or Private both support customer-managed KMS, VPC peering, and per-tenant audit logs. Default log retention 90d; enterprise retention is an add-on. I'll fill their questionnaire and flag: KMS rotation cadence, key separation, and approved egress endpoints.
Helix PM: We require AZ spread and a pre-scheduled warm SLA for campaign windows. Also need the burst credit cap option so we don't get surprise bills.
Ivy (solutions): For burst cap, we can set a hard budget on burst minutes and fail open to fallback model if exceeded. That gives predictable upper bound.
Marco (eng-infra): Action items: (1) I'll run the perf sim against Helix trace and produce A/B/C pricing and p50/p95/p99 latencies; (2) Tessa will draft a short warm/fallback runbook; (3) Lena will fill the security questionnaire; (4) Noah/Ivy will prepare the SOW language for burst cap + AZ spread.
cloud-bot: perf-sim job 1739991142 finished (status: success)
Marco (eng-infra): Quick sim summary uploaded: Option A (9 reserved) -> committed cost = $BASE_A/mo, median latency 100ms, p99 310ms. Option B (5 reserved + autoscale to 14) -> committed = $BASE_B/mo + ~$374/mo sample burst, median 140ms, p99 720ms. Option C (min commit + burst credits) -> $BASE_C/mo + ~$900/mo burst in sample month, median 210ms, p99 1.8s. Full CSV in shared drive.
Noah (sales): Great. I'll assemble a one-page deliverable with the three options, burst-cap language, and security answers. Setting status->waiting_on_customer for signed schedule + final trace confirmation.
Helix PM: Thanks everyone. We'll review and come back with preferred option and signed schedule next week. :thumbsup:
